title: Authorization
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of authorization and name the relevant Angular concepts.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on authorization inside Security and Privacy. Begin with the syllabus anchor “Roles and permissions”, name the data or UI behavior involved, and then verify the result with a focused example. The goal is to make one clear engineering decision rather than memorize an isolated API.
content.why_it_matters: Navigation and client-side UI decisions improve the experience, but they do not grant permission to protected backend resources. Server-side checks remain authoritative.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Authorization
content_blocks.code:
// UI navigation check only; the API must independently authorize the request.
export const canOpenAdmin = (role: string) => role === 'admin';
content_blocks.expected_output: Expected result: only the UI decision changes. Real permissions must be enforced by the trusted backend on every protected operation.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a snippet without checking its surrounding context.
common_mistakes.why: Angular examples can depend on imports, providers, template context or a particular framework version.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the run instructions and validate against the exact generated workspace.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating an attractive UI result as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Accessibility, boundary cases, failures and server-side rules may not be visible in the happy path.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a focused assertion and test at least one realistic failure state.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming client code guarantees authorization or validates all external data.
common_mistakes.why: Browser code is controlled by the client and can receive unexpected network responses.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate external values and enforce protected business rules on the backend.
